title: Prohibition on the Sale or Use of Coordinated Pricing Algorithms to Set Rents or Manage Occupancy Levels for Residential Dwelling Units
requirement: It shall be unlawful to sell, license, or otherwise provide to City of Berkeley landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley. landlords any coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy 
levels that may be achieved for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.

title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
requirement: Rental housing providers are prohibited from inquiring about criminal history, indicating that persons with criminal backgrounds will not be considered, refusing to rent or terminate tenancy based on criminal history, requiring disclosure or authorization for release of criminal history, demanding higher security deposits or rental amounts based on criminal history, refusing to allow addition of immediate family members based on criminal history, disqualifying tenants from rental assistance programs based on criminal history, or treating applicants or tenants differently based on criminal history. Landlords must provide written notice and opportunity to respond if taking any action against an applicant or tenant based on criminal history.
citation: BMC 13.106; Berkeley Rent Board ordinance passed April 14, 2020
quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
coverage_conditions: Legal city is Berkeley; applies to all rental housing providers in the city offering residential units for rent
exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; Public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); Owner-occupied properties with 1-3 units where owner of record resides as primary residence; Units under rental agreement allowing owner move-back per BMC 13.76.130 A.9; Units occupied by existing tenants seeking to sublet or add/replace roommates
sanctions: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times the amount of one month's rent; punitive damages; attorneys' fees and costs; injunctive relief

title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
requirement: Housing providers receiving Department of Neighborhood Development (DND) funding and/or land, or that have income restricted units created under the Boston Planning and Development Agency (BPDA) Inclusionary Development Policy will not impose a blanket policy that denies housing to anyone with arrests and or convictions. Housing providers will consider applicants on a case-by-case basis. The Developer/Agent agrees to not consider arrests that did not result in conviction (including dismissed charges, diversion programs, and similar non-convictions), convictions subject to judicial relief (expungement, sealing, certificates for relief from disabilities), juvenile records, or convictions more than 5 years old when determining housing eligibility.

title: General prohibition on rent control with limited municipal option under Chapter 40P Section 4
requirement: No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation only if: (1) after six months from initial adoption, compliance by property owners is entirely voluntary and uncoerced; (2) regulation may not include occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or removal of properties from regulation; (3) regulation may not apply to rental units owned by entities owning fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent exceeding $400; and (4) municipality must compensate owners for the difference between fair market rent and rent-controlled rent from general funds.
quoted_span:
No city or town may enact, maintain or enforce rent control of any kind, except that any city or town that accepts this chapter may adopt rent control regulation that provides:
(a) after six months from the date of the initial adoption of rent control regulation by a particular city or town, compliance on the part of property owners as to the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation shall be entirely voluntary and uncoerced, and the property of a person or entity declining to have his or its property subjected to such regulation shall be wholly unaffected by any aspect of the rent control regulation or any subsequently adopted rent control regulation;
(b) such regulation may not include the regulation of occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion or the removal of properties from such regulation, nor may such regulation apply to any rental unit that is owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units or that has a fair market rent exceeding $400; and
(c) a municipality adopting such regulation shall compensate owners of rent controlled units for each unit in the amount of the difference between the unit's fair market rent and the unit's below market, rent controlled rent, with such compensation coming from the municipality's general funds, so that the cost of any rent control shall be borne by all taxpayers of a municipality and not by the owners of regulated units only.
key_value: Massachusetts prohibits all rent control except for municipalities accepting Chapter 40P, which may regulate only multi-unit properties (≥10 units) with fair market rent ≤$400, with voluntary compliance after 6 months and mandatory municipal compensation from general funds.
coverage_conditions: Massachusetts state law applying to any city or town that accepts Chapter 40P and elects to adopt rent control regulation. Coverage is limited to rental units owned by entities owning ten or more rental units with fair market rent not exceeding $400.
exemptions: Exemptions apply to: (1) rental units owned by persons or entities owning fewer than ten rental units; (2) rental units with fair market rent exceeding $400; (3) after six months from initial adoption, property owners may opt out entirely and their property shall be wholly unaffected by the regulation. Regulation explicitly cannot regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal of properties from regulation.

title: Notice to Determine Estate at Will for Nonpayment of Rent
requirement: For nonpayment of rent on an estate at will, a landlord must provide fourteen days' written notice to quit. However, if a tenant has not received a similar notice within the preceding twelve months, the tenant may prevent termination by paying or tendering the full amount of rent due within ten days of receiving the notice. Every such notice must contain specific statutory notification language informing the tenant of this right; failure to include such notification extends the tenant's payment period to the day an answer is due in any possession action.
quoted_span: In case of neglect or refusal to pay the rent due from a tenant at will, fourteen days' notice to quit, given in writing by the landlord to the tenant, shall be sufficient to determine the tenancy; provided, that the tenancy of a tenant who has not received a similar notice from the landlord within the twelve months next preceding the receipt of such notice shall not be determined if the tenant, within ten days after the receipt thereof, pays or tenders to the landlord, the landlord's attorney, or the person to whom the tenant customarily pays rent, the full amount of any rent due.
